content.title: About
content.content: Lion's Mane mushroom (Hericium erinaceus) is an edible, polysaccharide‑rich fungus known for its potential nootropic benefits. It has a soft, slightly sweet texture and a flavor reminiscent of seafood or mild cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mushroom gets its name from the long, spiny “mane” that looks like a lion's hair.
In traditional Chinese medicine, lion's mane has been used to support the nervous system and improve cognition.
It grows on dead or weakened hardwoods, especially birch and oak.
Beta‑glucan content in lion's mane is higher than in most edible mushrooms.
In Japan it is often added to tea or prepared as a broth.

items.title: Nerve support
items.content: Lion's Mane extracts stimulate nerve growth factor (NGF) production, which may help memory and concentration.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory
items.content: Beta‑glucans and erinacines exhibit anti‑inflammatory effects, aiding in the reduction of chronic inflammation.

items.title: Immune boost
items.content: Polysaccharides enhance macrophage activity and increase the body's resistance to infections.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: The mushroom provides dietary fiber that supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience skin rash or itching after consuming the mushroom.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Lion's Mane may enhance the effects of anticoagulants; consult a physician if you take blood thinners.

items.title: Product quality
items.content: Low‑quality or contaminated supplements can contain heavy metals or mycotoxins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The mushroom can be eaten fresh, sautéed, stewed, or added to soups and sauces. Dried caps are often ground into powder for capsules or tea. Before cooking, rinse and slice into large pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh mushrooms in a paper bag in the refrigerator for 3–5 days. Dried mushrooms keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 12 months. Discard if mold or off‑odors develop.
